We married young as well. I was 20 and my wife was 18. Our 17 year anniversary is coming up on July 31st. But, I am by no means an expert.
My personal opinion is no secrets. Keeping stuff from each other always ends badly.
Treat each other as equal, both as adults and in parenting roles. Discuss finances together. No matter which one is the sole provider, neither wants to be in the dark about money.
Show interest in each others hobbies or passions. Even if it bores you to tears. Listen to each others problems and worries. Sometimes people just want to be heard.
Lastly, make time for romance. People can live without sex, but it is hard to live without feeling loved. A side note, I work overnight and have most of our marriage. I think that has kept our alone time more special. Three kids later we need it for sure.

Not one but three:

  • Talk about your needs, problems, stuff that makes you mad or you need help with. No one can read your mind, spouse included.
  • Try to replace each other when doing common tasks now and then, this will not only teach you to say thank you but also value job done and respect each other commitment.
  • Find at least one hobby you'll do together. It's important to share fun and have pleasant memories of time spent together.

Universal advice for any relationship: Listen to your partner (don't just hear them, fucking LISTEN), communicate your wants & needs appropriately, treat them with respect but don't bow down to demands.

But my absolute, final piece of advice is this: Set rules and goals for you and your partner. Those can be elaborated on or changed over time if necessary, but communicating these simple things can save a lot of headaches further down the road.

Don't give up. In 50 years you will not care about the million+ reasons you might have wanted to split up along the way, but you will remember the good+bad times and be greatful to have someone with you through it all.

Don't hold grudges. Argue, go to bed, wake up the next day with everything forgotten.
